top10.name: Rakazo
top10.tagline: The open source Grok Bot alternative you actually own

real_comment_themes.praise: A fast-paced, incredible open-source Grok Bot alternative that allows bringing any model or sandbox provider, supports ChatGPT, and is highly recommended for personal and customer work. Self-hosting is a big deal for client documents.
real_comment_themes.concerns_or_questions: Is it possible to add integration to a marketplace? Is there a per-bot spend cap? What about a short daily report per agent, what it did, what it skipped, and why? Can one bring their own models? Do routines check in while long-running work is in progress?

top10.name: Frevana Multiplayer
top10.tagline: AI that grows your business alongside your team

real_comment_themes.praise: The multiplayer idea is great for sharing AI agents and turning one person's workflow into a team resource, saving a lot of time. The ability to tweak and share agents is useful, and the support for BYOK and integration with SaaS apps is appreciated.
real_comment_themes.concerns_or_questions: Is there an example of the actual output? How easy is it to share custom skills? How is the interface designed for agent-human interaction? If an agent is shared, is access to connected tools also shared? What happens if someone edits a shared skill? Does the whole team get it? Does anyone get pinged when a teammate changes a shared skill? Can one set an owner per agent task to approve output?

top10.name: Tulvo
top10.tagline: Smart & adaptive workspace to manage all your work

real_comment_themes.praise: A promising product that can describe a business in one sentence and generate working boards and customer tables. The ability to update the workspace from various sources and connect to a single dataset is a standout feature.
real_comment_themes.concerns_or_questions: How is it different from other platforms that generate web apps? How hard is it to get data out if a team outgrows it? What happens when the AI makes a change to an existing database? Is there a way to review or undo structural changes? Can it turn meeting notes into tasks?

top10.name: Talyn
top10.tagline: Run Claude Code and Codex in parallel cloud sandboxes

real_comment_themes.praise: A very interesting product that helps automate the babysitting of AI code, especially for fixing failing checks. The detail of tokens staying outside the sandbox and the caching of boxes for faster startups are appreciated.
real_comment_themes.concerns_or_questions: When it fixes a failing check, does one see the diff before it pushes? Does it ever run out of GitHub API budget? How are secrets handled in the sandbox? Where does one see it when the AI stops to ask a question? What happens when two parallel processes touch the same file? Do parallel sandboxes share repo context, or does each agent re-read the whole repo?

top10.name: HuntMonitor
top10.note: not in the 00:05 list (added later); no text held

real_comment_themes.praise: A useful tool with a clean, simple, and accurate interface for monitoring Product Hunt launches.
real_comment_themes.concerns_or_questions: Does it cover products that are featured? Is it just logging data, or does it have insider intel? Could it have automated alerts for momentum changes or ranking drops, and weekly performance reports? Does it get around Product Hunt's upvote visibility restriction? Does it show votes per hour? Which numbers are worth watching for a first-time launcher?

top10.name: Canvas by AgentGrid.io
top10.tagline: Agentic Design Canvas - A visual way to collaborate with AI

real_comment_themes.praise: A fantastic and useful tool that makes building with AI easier, especially for visual collaboration. The idea of the canvas as a shared state is a real difference from chat-style tools.
real_comment_themes.concerns_or_questions: When one fixes something by hand, and the agent picks up again, does it see the edit or can it overwrite it? What happens when one and the agent change the same element at the same time? Can existing Tailwind config be loaded to stick to a spacing scale? How does the handoff work when taking a design from Canvas into one's own codebase?

top10.name: TwoBucket
top10.tagline: Beginner-friendly mobile detailing software for bookings

real_comment_themes.praise: A well-niched product for mobile detailers, with deposits and tips built-in. The focus on a specific solo operator group is appreciated.
real_comment_themes.concerns_or_questions: Is there a way to move a whole day's visits at once and let customers pick new slots? Could it include AI-powered vehicle inspection? How are the first users being found? How does a detailer who has never used booking software get started easily?

top10.name: Perit Marketplace
top10.tagline: Sell your data and RL tasks to frontier AI labs

top10.name: Remindly
top10.tagline: Notes that remind you, on iPhone, iPad, Mac and web

real_comment_themes.praise: A useful tool for notes with reminders, especially for specific use cases like recipes with fold timers. The location-based reminders and offline functionality are nice touches.
real_comment_themes.concerns_or_questions: Does the 'arrive somewhere' reminder work on iPad too? Does the Evernote import bring over existing reminders or only text and tags? Do repeating reminders still go off if the phone has no signal?

top10.name: Spiik
top10.tagline: AI note taker for meetings & lectures. No bot on your calls.

real_comment_themes.praise: A helpful AI note-taker for meetings and lectures, especially the feature to tap any line to hear it again. The ability to ask the recording questions is also highly valued.
real_comment_themes.concerns_or_questions: How does the 'no bot' feature work on Mac, specifically regarding system audio and mic as separate tracks? Does speaker labeling hold up with multiple people using one laptop mic? Do flashcards work from a full hour of audio without prior transcript editing? Can one ask questions across several recordings at once?
